name: Oway
long_description:
The physical economy still operates without a common language. Enterprise systems, factories, trucks, and robots generate enormous amounts of data, but most remains fragmented across legacy software and incompatible formats. Without a shared understanding of what is happening, even the most advanced AI cannot reliably coordinate how goods are made, moved, and delivered.

Oway is building that common language. Our protocol, IOI, connects enterprise systems and physical hardware, cleaning messy legacy data and live telemetry into a standardized schema that AI can understand and act on. Through a shared API, businesses can query their operations, identify inefficiencies, and automate actions across systems without replacing their existing software.

Our first model, Juno, applies this intelligence to unused truck capacity. It tracks empty space on trucks and sells it at a 50% discount to businesses shipping in the same direction. By moving freight directly on trucks already making the trip, Oway reduces shipping costs, damage, and transit times while generating additional revenue for carriers.

Every connected system and shipment expands our understanding of capacity, pricing, routes, facilities, and industrial operations. As this network grows, Oway is building toward a future where enterprise software, automated factories, self-driving vehicles, and robots can communicate and coordinate through one shared layer, making the physical economy programmable.
one_liner: Building the open operating system for the automated physical economy.

launches.title: Oway: Building the Internet of Industrials
launches.tagline: Oway connects industrial systems through a common protocol, giving AI the context to coordinate the physical economy.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re building the Internet of Industrials (IOI), a shared context layer connecting industrial systems and giving AI a common basis of structured data across companies. IOI already powers Oway, where our first model, Juno, uses it to coordinate shipments through unused truck capacity. We’re opening that same foundation to robotics, automated factories and other industrial systems to accelerate US industrial automation.

![](/media/?type=post&id=122375&key=user_uploads/993914/9346b6ba-f710-49c9-9ecb-72882cc13bca)

**An example:** A factory asks its AI for eight units of mild steel by tomorrow morning. Through IOI, the AI coordinates production with a connected certified supplier and books a connected truck for delivery. All three systems share the context needed to execute and track the order.

### The problem

America is building new factories, deploying automation, and developing autonomous vehicles. But the systems connecting industrial operations still speak different languages.

Inventory, capacity, equipment, orders, and operating constraints are scattered across ERP systems, TMSs, warehouses, carriers, sensors, and closed systems. That fragmentation extends across the companies that need to work together. AI cannot reliably coordinate physical work without understanding what exists, what is available, and what each system can do.

Productive capacity goes unused while businesses pay more to make, store, and move goods.

### Introducing IOI

We built IOI as the backend that runs Oway. It already connects every Oway customer and carrier. We’re now making it available to other businesses as a common structured context layer.

Our thesis is that logistics provides the foundational language for an industrial network. Nearly every physical business can be described through a common set of primitives: **what exists, where it is, where it needs to go, available capacity, time, cost, constraints, storage, and transformation.**

IOI translates those states into structured data that enterprise software, physical hardware and AI agents can share across company boundaries. Businesses can build nodes alongside their existing systems instead of replacing them. 

Setting up an IOI node is extremely simple, our default setup allows you to simply plug Oway in as a “carrier” into your stack that monitors and optimizes your supply chain quotes and orders - automatically gaining the context to build a full IOI data lake for you that already has action capabilities and can infer your inventory levels and SKU-level performance. Data can then automatically be fed back to SAP, Oracle Netsuite, or any data system / AI agent you’d like.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122375&key=user_uploads/993914/c9f841f6-3976-429b-9f25-81e63bc0c113)

IOI will be open source soon, with Oway maintaining the standard so developers can build compatible systems. It is designed around widely adopted enterprise security practices, with each business controlling its data, access permissions and authorized actions. Nodes can run in enterprise clouds or at the edge.

**Below: Ask IOI anything -** Each Oway enterprise customer also gets search functionality out of the box. 

![](/media/?type=post&id=122375&key=user_uploads/993914/07bea764-9c83-47a6-8c71-97f5130d28b5)

### Our first model: Juno

Juno is our first AI model. It reasons over IOI to price, coordinate and execute pooled shipments on trucks already traveling the route.

By ridesharing shipments into capacity already moving, we lower costs, shorten transit times and reduce damage from handling. Carriers earn from their existing capacity, with legal paperwork, insurance and DOT compliance all automatically monitored and handled.

**Below: Juno in Oway OS.** A full API, MCP and EDI-compatible suite that enables businesses to leverage Juno’s rideshare capabilities however they’d like for freight shipping.

![](/media/?type=post&id=122375&key=user_uploads/993914/f2a8e9b3-a635-4c69-b9a8-4c5d3f8eb1f7)

We estimate this is a **$200B+ annual optimization opportunity within America’s roughly $1T trucking industry**.

With Oway Rideshare, we deliver average savings of 30% per transaction, while also reducing damage rates, and transit times as well for cross-country shipments.

Freight gives IOI an operating environment where its primitives have to produce real physical outcomes.

### Where we’re going

Every connected system and shipment adds context about capacity, pricing, routes, facilities, and industrial operations.

That shared context gives robotics companies, automated factories and self-driving trucks a way to communicate and coordinate across companies. Every company on Oway, and even Oway’s model - are already running on IOI. We believe that providing these capabilities at a national level will lead to significant improvements to the GDP and global competitiveness of US-made products.

Oway + IOI already serves Fortune 500 companies, connects over 10,000 vehicles nationwide, and indexes hundreds of millions of dollars in annualized shipping demand.

If you’re working at a company that makes, stores, or moves physical goods, [we’d love to show you what we’re building](https://www.shipoway.com).
